cards.english: She can't swim.
Mom always does laundry.
cards.existing: `Весь (Ves)/вся/всё/все` covers 'all', 'the whole', 'everyone', 'everything' depending on form. Context + ending tells you which.

cards.english: He is twenty-five years old.
They're two of a kind.
May I ask you a question?
cards.existing: `Надо` (Nado) and `нужно` = 'need to / should'. Person goes dative: `Мне надо идти` (I need to go – literally 'to-me necessary to-go'). The 'subject' is in dative.

cards.english: I don't like this movie.
cards.existing: `Нравиться` (Nravit'sya) flips the subject and object: `Мне нравится книга` literally = 'to-me appeals book' = 'I like the book'. The thing liked is the grammatical subject.

cards.english: He doesn't work on weekends.
They couldn't solve the problem.
You shouldn't talk so loudly.
cards.existing: `Можно` (one can/may) and `нельзя` (one can't/may not) are impersonal: `Здесь можно курить?` (Can one smoke here?). No subject needed.

cards.english: The bus comes every fifteen minutes.
cards.existing: `Каждый` (every) and `весь` (all/whole) act like adjectives – match gender, number, case. `Каждый день` (m, nom), `всю ночь` (f, acc).

cards.english: Hello, how are you?
cards.existing: Possessives precede the noun: `мой дом` (moy dom), not `дом мой`. Putting it after sounds emphatic or poetic.

cards.english: A kind man is standing on the corner.
The middle of summer is vacation time.
Five children are playing in the yard.

cards.target: Она никогда не жалуется на работу.
cards.english: She never complains about work.

cards.target: У меня нет времени на это.
cards.english: I don't have time for this.

cards.target: Мы не согласны с этим решением.
cards.english: We don't agree with this decision.

cards.target: Тебе не стоит волноваться из-за экзамена.
cards.english: You shouldn't worry about the exam.

cards.target: Высокое здание построили в прошлом году.
cards.english: A tall building was built last year.

cards.target: Продавец пел песню на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The salesman sang a song last week.

cards.target: Она слушает классическую музыку каждый вечер.
cards.english: She listens to classical music every evening.
cards.existing: Frequency adverbs `всегда` (always), `никогда` (never) don't change shape. They sit before the verb: `я всегда читаю`.

cards.target: Ребёнок ездит в школу каждое утро.
cards.english: The child goes to school every morning.
Today is the twenty-fifth of March.
The farmer picks apples in autumn.
Warm milk helps you fall asleep.
The female teacher praises diligent children.
This is the fifth chapter of the book.
It takes forty minutes to drive to the airport.
The kitchen smells of fresh baking.
The architect washes dishes before bed.
The deep sea holds many secrets.
A cheerful song plays on the radio.
A cheerful clown is standing on the corner.
The athlete usually works in the office.
There are twenty-five students in the class.
The teacher explained the rule several times.
A strong wind is blowing from the sea.
The teacher explains a difficult topic to the students.

cards.target: Не могли бы вы закрыть окно?
cards.english: Would you mind closing the window?
cards.existing: `Бы` (By) can sit anywhere after the verb or pronoun: `Я бы пошёл`, `я пошёл бы`, `пошёл бы я`. Position is flexible – meaning stays the same.

cards.target: Бабушка готовит вкусный суп по воскресеньям.
cards.english: Grandma cooks delicious soup on Sundays.

cards.target: Не трогай чужие вещи без разрешения.
cards.english: Don't touch other people's things without permission.

cards.target: Он заказал горячий суп в ресторане.
cards.english: He ordered hot soup at the restaurant.

cards.target: Бабушка вяжет тёплый шарф для внука.
cards.english: Grandmother knits a warm scarf for her grandson.

cards.target: Я не понимаю, можете повторить, пожалуйста?
cards.english: I don't understand, can you repeat that please?

cards.target: Сосед плавал в бассейне на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The neighbor swam in the pool last week.

cards.target: Здравствуйте, меня зовут Иван, очень приятно познакомиться.
cards.english: Hello, my name is Ivan, very nice to meet you.
cards.existing: Asking: `Как тебя зовут?` (informal) or `Как вас зовут?` (formal). Literally 'How do they call you?'. The name comes back: `Меня зовут [name]`.

cards.target: Он нигде не может найти свои ключи.
cards.english: He can't find his keys anywhere.
cards.existing: `Свой` (Svoy) agrees with the noun it modifies in gender/number/case, just like other possessives. `Свой дом` (m), `своя машина` (f), `своё окно` (n).

cards.target: Ни ты, ни я не знаем правду.
cards.english: Neither you nor I know the truth.
cards.existing: Feminine doesn't care about animacy in the accusative singular: `женщину` (zhenshchinu), `книгу` – both end in `-у/-ю` regardless. The rule applies to masc + all plurals.

cards.target: Русский язык – один из самых сложных.
cards.english: Russian is one of the most difficult languages.

cards.target: Мой номер телефона записан в этой тетради.
cards.english: My phone number is written in this notebook.

cards.target: Я учусь в университете на третьем курсе.
cards.english: I study at the university in the third year.

cards.target: Садовник посадил лаванду и подсолнухи в палисаднике.
cards.english: The gardener planted lavender and sunflowers in the front garden.

cards.target: Добрый день, вы не подскажете дорогу к метро?
cards.english: Good afternoon, could you tell me the way to the metro?

cards.target: Три раза в неделю я хожу в спортзал.
cards.english: Three times a week I go to the gym.

cards.target: Извините, вы не подскажете, где находится ближайшая аптека?
cards.english: Excuse me, could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?
cards.existing: Some imperatives are irregular: `дать (dat') → дай`, `есть → ешь`. Memorize the common ones; they appear constantly in everyday speech.

cards.target: В году двенадцать месяцев и триста шестьдесят пять дней.
cards.english: There are twelve months and three hundred sixty-five days in a year.

cards.target: Они строили дом два года и наконец построили его.
cards.english: They built a house over two years.

cards.target: Почтальон ехал на велосипеде под дождём с полной сумкой.
cards.english: The postman rode his bicycle through the rain with a full bag.
cards.existing: Walking vs vehicle: `идти (idti)/ходить` for on foot, `ехать/ездить` for any vehicle. Russian distinguishes how you move, English doesn't.

cards.english: The salesperson helps customers choose gifts.
A fresh apple is in the basket.

cards.target: Архитектор покупал продукты на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The architect bought groceries last week.

cards.target: Токарь выточил деревянную чашу на токарном станке.
cards.english: The turner shaped a wooden bowl on the lathe.

cards.target: Двадцать третьего февраля – День защитника Отечества.
cards.english: The twenty-third of February is Defender of the Fatherland Day.
